title: document.getElementById only finds connected nodes — capture the element ref BEFORE removing its ancestor, not after
trigger: Cleanup code removes a wrapper/ancestor element, then tries to re-query or restore a descendant via document.getElementById/querySelector — the descendant was detached along with the ancestor so the lookup returns null and the restore silently never runs
principle: getElementById and document.querySelector only search connected DOM. If a teardown removes an ancestor (wrapper.remove(), innerHTML reset, framework re-render) before you look up a child that must survive, the lookup returns null and the element is orphaned forever — the UI surface vanishes with no error. Fix ordering: capture the element reference while it is still connected (refs survive detachment; queries do not), move it to its restore target, THEN remove the ancestor. When the restore target itself may have been re-rendered away, fall back to a connected alternative before appendChild (target.isConnected guard).

cases.context: Split View close on m.youtube (any site): cleanup ran wrapper.remove() — detaching stageTihoka which held #Tihoka-subtitle-root — then read document.getElementById('Tihoka-subtitle-root') to move it back. Null → restore skipped → subtitle overlay permanently gone until next full re-mount.
cases.bad:
wrapper?.remove(); // detaches stageTihoka + TihokaRoot
const TihokaRoot = document.getElementById('Tihoka-subtitle-root'); // null!
if (TihokaRoot) target.appendChild(TihokaRoot); // never runs

applyFor: Any teardown that removes a container and must preserve/re-parent descendants
Deferred cleanup (post-animation restore) where the subtree may detach before the restore runs
Reviewing 'element disappeared after closing X' bugs — check removal vs re-query ordering first
